text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The number of new companies increased in Sweden for the third consecutive year. In 1996, 28,000 companies were set up, creating 50,000 new jobs, figures from Statistics Sweden and state venture capital provider Nutek shows. About two percent of the companies filed for bankruptcy in the same year.
- Household appliance group Electrolux will reduce staff by 12,000 over the next two or three years by closing 25 plants.
- The Stockholm Stock Exchange and the Copenhagen bourse will cooperate to strengthen their positions.

- Foreign exchange fluctuations have made it more expensive for Swedes to go on vacation abroad, particularly if they are heading for the U.S. and Britain as the dollar and sterling have strengthened while the crown has softened.
- Household appliance group Electrolux's shares rose 14 percent after news its new chief executive Michael Treschow will close 25 plants and cut staff by 12,000 employees.

- Wage inflation is a threat to Sweden, the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) said. The Paris-based group said growth and state finances are on the right track while wage formation could throw a spanner into the works.
- Norwegian petrol group Statoil will invest up to five billion crowns in shopping centres connected to their Swedish service stations, sources told the newspaper.
- Swedish automotive group Volvo will expand through organic growth and company acquisitions, Leif Johansson, group chief executive, told investors at a seminar.
- The process of restructuring and rationalising the steel and forestry industries will continue, Bo Berggren, chariman of forestry group Stora told a steel industry seminar.
